git.source_digest_rule: sha256 over name+bytes of src/trading_bot/research/edge01/*.py, scripts/edge01_run.py and scripts/edge01_verify.py, with CRLF folded to LF so the digest does not depend on the checkout's line endings

mode: deterministic backtest over the local historical corpus; the DEV window decides, VAL and OOS confirm; 0 orders, 0 credentials, 0 network calls

experiment.question: H2 measured the intraday book paying for the extension: 236 of 290 DEV fills landed at or past 0.25 ATR above the broken level and only the fills closest to the level carried positive gross. Does entering on a resting limit AT the level — same signals, same stop, same target, same risk budget, same costs — improve the net expectancy, and are the orders actually filled?

arms.frozen_market: the frozen EDGE-INTRA-01 ruleset, market entry at the next bar's open (the published WP arm, re-run here as the baseline of this experiment)
arms.plan_market: the SAME plans the retest arm would rest, crossed at market: it isolates how much of the difference is the plan's own gate numbers and how much is the execution price
arms.plan_limit: the same plans rested as limit buys at the broken level, live for the declared expiry, filled only if a bar trades at or through the level, at the level and never better

variant_params.entry: resting limit buy at the broken level (hard_invalidation)
variant_params.fill_rule: a bar whose low reaches the level fills it, at the level, never better
variant_params.cancellation: a close below the level cancels the plan; the window end cancels it

unreachable_outcomes.cancelled_close_below_level: a bar that closes below the level has traded at or through it by construction (low <= close < level), so it fills first: the plan's own invalidation cannot cancel a resting order at that level. The branch stays in the book as a guard and the verifier checks that the outcome never appears

economic_rule.RETEST_UNPOWERED: fewer orders placed or fills than the declared floors
economic_rule.RETEST_IMPROVES_NET: net AND expectancy per trade both better than the baseline
economic_rule.RETEST_IMPROVES_EXPECTANCY_ONLY: expectancy per trade better, net not better
economic_rule.RETEST_DOES_NOT_HELP: neither net nor expectancy better than the baseline

execution_rule.VIABLE: at least the declared share of the placed orders was filled
execution_rule.STARVED: the plan cannot be executed often enough to matter, whatever its P&L

decision_rule.not_claimed: a favourable economic reading is a hypothesis for a new pre-registered run, not a promotion: nothing is wired into the PAPER runtime and the ruleset in candidates.FROZEN_PARAMS is unchanged

market_context.timeframe: 1d (aggregated from 1h shards; a day exists only when its 24 contiguous hours do)
market_context.rule: benchmark BTC daily close against its own 200-day EMA, with that EMA's 20-day change deciding trend from range: BULL when close > EMA200 and the EMA rose over the last 20 days, BEAR when close < EMA200 and it fell, SIDEWAYS otherwise, UNDEFINED while either input is still warming up. This is the project's existing convention (trading_bot/research/swing/backtest.py::build_regimes), reused rather than re-invented; it is a market label for reporting, never a signal.

VAL.note: confirmatory window: the plan's rules were frozen before any of the three windows was run under H6 and nothing was re-tuned after reading it, but the diagnosis that motivated the plan came from DEV, so DEV is its design window and this one is evidence, not a decision

OOS.note: confirmatory window: the plan's rules were frozen before any of the three windows was run under H6 and nothing was re-tuned after reading it, but the diagnosis that motivated the plan came from DEV, so DEV is its design window and this one is evidence, not a decision

limitations: the signals are the frozen candidate's, so this experiment cannot be better than the signals it inherits: it isolates the entry price, not the setup

a limit that fills only when price comes back is filled precisely when the breakout is failing — adverse selection. Without a historical order book the model cannot charge for it, so the fill is charged the SAME spread, slippage, impact and fee as a market entry and the limit is always filled at the level, never better

queue position is not modelled: a bar that merely touches the level is treated as a fill. That is the optimistic side of the fill rule, and it is why the fill rate is published per order rather than assumed
the expiry (8 bars of 15m) is declared here and was not tuned: a longer window would fill more orders at prices further from the diagnosis
the risk budget is consulted at the moment of the touch, so an order can be cancelled by a refusal the market arm would never have met; those orders are published with the refusal reason
single corpus window per split; no historical order book; long side only (spot)
